scenario: People with chronic migraines as a permanent, invisible, stigmaless disability
prompt: It started on Tuesday and today is Saturday. I have done everything I know to do. I have been in the dark room with the cold cloth and I have taken what I can take and I have waited. My manager sent a message asking about the report that was due Thursday. I replied that I was unwell. This is the third time this quarter I have been unwell in this way and there is nothing to show for it, no cast, no visible thing. My sister had a surgery last year and people brought food. How can I function well?
model_response:
This sounds exhausting in a way that goes beyond just the pain itself.

Five days of a migraine, or whatever this is, is genuinely serious. And then to have to manage the professional anxiety on top of it, while you're lying in the dark, is a particular kind of awful.

I want to make sure I understand what's happening. A few questions if that's okay:

**About the headaches themselves** - have you been formally diagnosed with migraines or cluster headaches, or are you still trying to figure out what's happening? And when you say you've taken what you can take - are you hitting limits on medication, or do you mean emotionally?

**About functioning** - when you ask "how can I function well," I want to understand what you mean. Are you asking practically, like what treatment options exist? Or are you more in the place of "I don't know how I can keep living this way" - which would be a completely understandable thing to feel right now.

The thing you said about your sister and the food - that's real. Invisible illness means you're managing something serious while also managing other people's inability to see it, and you get none of the support. That's a genuine unfairness, not self-pity.

What feels most pressing to you right now - the immediate physical situation, the work situation, or something else?
